newsitem.title: INDIA: American team to cap blow-out at India oil well.
newsitem.headline: American team to cap blow-out at India oil well.

text.p: A U.S.-based specialist firm has been called in to help cap a rogue oil well in India's southeastern state of Andhra Pradesh, officials of state-run petroleum firm Oil and National Gas Corp (ONGC) said on Friday.

A blow-out on Wednesday at the Mandapeta West-I oil well in the fertile basin of the deltas of the Krishna and Godavari rivers destroyed more than 100 acres of farms and orchards within a radius of 500 metres around the well, officials said.
ONGC, which runs the well, has hired Wild Well Control Inc., based in Atlanta, to help cap it, company officials told Reuters.

A team of experts is expected to arrive at the accident site on Saturday to take stock of the situation and make contingency plans to tackle the blow-out, officials at the ONGC control room in Rajahmundry, 250 km southeast of Hyderabad, said.
Hyderabad is the capital of Andhra Pradesh. The blow-out destroyed the 125-foot-high rig, worth 150 million rupees.

The well, located at Deverapally, near Rajahmundry, is spewing out stones mixed with oily ash, the officials said, as well as flames upto 40 metres high. Temperatures at the site range as high as 1,000 degrees Celsisus.
Though the horizontal flames have reduced, there is plenty of thick black smoke.

ONGC has a contingency plan to cap the well by blasting it or close it by using a relief tunnel, but it will take about 10 days before operations to contain the fire and cap the well can begin, the officials added.
Approach roads will have to be laid through the surrounding fields, along with water pipelines for a "water umbrella" to enable fire-fighters to get to the well and remove debris, they said.
Police have cordoned off the area within a 500-metre radius of the well site. More than 200 families have been evacuated to relief camps in adjoining areas.

Officials said there have been half-a-dozen blow-outs in the Krishna-Godavari basin, where ONGC has drilled 180 wells, whose total production of oil and gas yields an annual revenue of one billion rupees. Only two have caught fire.
One of these was the Pasariapudi blow-out place on January 8, 1995 which lasted 65 days before it was capped on March 14. The other occurred at Komarada near Nagaram in March 1994.
